We reviewed your requirements for architecting a production **Model Context Protocol (MCP) server in Rust** with **hybrid LLM routing (Ollama + Gemini Flash)** and **PostgreSQL `pgvector` semantic memory**.

## 1. Executive Project Pitch & Technical Abstract (NSF Project Pitch / Portal Format)

**Technical Abstract:**  
Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) adopting autonomous AI agents face two systemic barriers: prohibitive cloud token expenditure for continuous multi-step workflows, and severe security vulnerabilities (arbitrary command injection, unauthorized filesystem traversal, and credential exfiltration) inherent in unsandboxed tool-calling frameworks. **Digital Nomad LLC** proposes a 6-month NSF SBIR Phase I R&D project to advance **Agent Smith (`claw-mcp-server v0.2.0`)**, our operational **TRL-6/TRL-7 Rust Hybrid Multi-Agent Orchestrator**, into an open-standards, verifiable enterprise automation runtime. Built in **Rust (Edition 2024, Tokio async, RMCP 1.7)** coupled with a **Python 3.14 `SQLModel` worker plane** and **PostgreSQL 16 + `pgvector 0.8.7` (768-dim HNSW cosine indexing)**, the proposed system introduces three core technical innovations: (1) a deterministic **Hybrid Inference & Zero-Token Pre-Scoring Router** that pairs sub-millisecond `pgvector` capability matching and local small-language-model inference (`qwen2.5-coder:1.5b`) with multi-model cloud foundation fallbacks, cutting cloud API costs by $>70\%$; (2) a zero-trust **Rust Capability Sandbox (`SandboxConfig::resolve_safe_path`)** enforcing path canonicalization, binary allowlists, and non-blocking execution checkpoints across 17+ native Model Context Protocol (MCP) tools; and (3) a shared **768-Dimensional Collective Vector Memory** uniting compiled Rust control planes and Python analytical workers with zero schema drift. ## 1. Executive Project Pitch & Technical Abstract (250-Word SBIR Portal Format)

**Technical Abstract:**  
During natural disasters and humanitarian crises, vulnerable populations and first responders face severe information fragmentation regarding emergency shelter capacity, medical aid, food distribution, and potable water—compounded by degraded cellular connectivity. **Digital Nomad LLC** proposes a 9-month SBIR Phase I project to advance our existing **TRL-6 cross-platform civic resource navigation architecture (`Shelter Source` & `Nomad Nexus`)** to **TRL-7 operational field readiness**. Built on a unified **Flutter/Dart** codebase for iOS, Android, and Web backed by **Firebase Auth, Cloud Firestore, and local offline-first persistence**, the platform delivers three core innovations: (1) high-throughput geospatial indexing and real-time filtering across heterogeneous humanitarian resource layers (<2s map load for 100+ regional nodes); (2) deterministic offline-first local storage with automated background synchronization and conflict resolution achieving $\ge 95\%$ sync integrity across intermittent connectivity regimes; and (3) a multi-tiered community crowdsourcing and peer/moderator verification pipeline enforced via granular Firestore security rules and reputation weighting ($\ge 80\%$ automated verification throughput under simulated 1,000-user load). Phase I culminates in a 20-operator field pilot with partner NGOs and municipal emergency managers, establishing dual-use commercialization pathways across FEMA/municipal disaster response SaaS and daily civic resource navigation.
